clue.text: One that's organised stamp store?

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters of the two words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle about whoever keeps a shop of stamps in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: 'organised' rearranges STAMP STORE, and the whole sentence describes the person in charge of a post office, a place that stores and sells stamps.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a post office is the official who runs a place stocking and selling postage stamps.

clue.text: Press being offensive

definitions.meaning: to press is to shove or force forward
a military offensive, a big advance

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means shove; as a noun it is a concerted military attack.

clue.text: Capable runner, fellow in period of calm almost

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow, like a sledge runner

indicators.note: in places the fellow inside the shortened calm word
almost says the last letter of the calm word is dropped

parts.note: a lull is a quiet spell

explanation.surface: An able athlete, a man in a near-quiet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LULL to LUL; 'in' puts F inside it. 'Runner' looks like an athlete but is a ski.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone capable has skill and competence at a task.

clue.text: Dean terms tutu out of order for particular kind of learner

indicators.note: out of order means not in the right sequence, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A college dean decrees ballet skirts unacceptable for a certain student.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult who enters higher education later in life than usual.

clue.text: Underwater mariner, perhaps, not fully evolved

parts.note: sub is short for submarine, an underwater vessel
a sailor is an example of a person

explanation.surface: A deep-sea sailor seems a primitive form of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underwater mariner' looks like a submariner, but splits into the vessel and a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking the qualities of a person, below the level of full development.

clue.text: Avoid overture, eschewing publicity

indicators.note: eschewing means shunning, so the publicity letters are removed

parts.note: a prelude is an introductory piece of music
PR is public relations, publicity

explanation.surface: A shy performer skips the opening number to stay out of the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to escape or evade something cleverly.

clue.text: Check flower feature

definitions.meaning: to check a flow is to stop or stanch it
the stalk that supports a bloom

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means stop or hold back; as a noun it is the stalk of a plant.

clue.text: Catch when touring river a few drops

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the catch word encloses the river letter

parts.note: a tickle is a catch or irritation in the throat

explanation.surface: An angler grabs a fish while touring a river with little water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests fishing but means a tickle in the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin slow flow of liquid, only small amounts at a time.

clue.text: Anthem lord composed in place of origin

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so these letters form a new word

explanation.surface: A nobleman writes a national song where he was born.
explanation.definitionFit: One's native country, the land a person was born in.

clue.text: Period at work in loose dress

definitions.meaning: a stretch of working hours, like a night turn
a simple straight dress hanging loosely from the shoulders

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a spell of duty in a workplace and a plain unfitted frock.

clue.text: Model sportsman with run seconds away

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

indicators.note: away tells us the seconds are sent off from the run word

parts.note: to sprint is to run fast

explanation.surface: A fashion model who is also an athlete, apparently able to run in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes S (seconds) from SPRINT, leaving PRINT. A Blue is an Oxbridge sporting award, and by extension the athlete who holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed plan or template that something else is based on, as in a blueprint for reform.

clue.text: Cite no imports for review — as evidence of this?

definitions.text: Cite no imports for review — as evidence of this?

indicators.note: for review means the letters are re-examined and recast in a new order

explanation.surface: A trade policy is judged by whether a review mentions no foreign goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for review' rearranges CITENOIMPORTS; the whole clue then describes the policy, since naming no imports would point to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic policy of shielding home industry by restricting or taxing foreign goods.

clue.text: Chef among retinue of rogue making Chinese speciality

indicators.note: among means the chef word is placed in the middle of the other letters
rogue as a verb-like adjective here signals the letters going astray into a new arrangement

parts.note: a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: A cook mingling with an unruly entourage produces a Chinese dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' here is an anagram signal (gone astray), rearranging the retinue's letters with OF to give FORTUNEIE; 'among' then places the chef inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp biscuit holding a printed prophecy, served in Chinese restaurants in the West.

clue.text: Examine container carried aboard Sweden pleasure trip

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

indicators.note: carried aboard means the container is taken inside the ship-like pieces

parts.note: a cruise is a holiday voyage
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: Customs inspect a can brought onto a Swedish holiday ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to inspect closely and thoroughly.

clue.text: Huge damage found in a product of mine

indicators.note: found in says the damage word sits inside the mine product

parts.note: coal is dug out of a mine
damage in the sense of a loss suffered

explanation.surface: Enormous harm is discovered in something extracted from a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something gigantic or enormous in size.

clue.text: Cancel engineers, leading to ding-dong

indicators.note: leading to puts the engineers before the bells

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
the ringing of bells, a peal

explanation.surface: Engineers call off a job that would end in a noisy row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ding-dong' looks like a quarrel (a British slang sense) but here it is the sound of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke a law or order officially is to annul it.

clue.text: Forceful old soldier defending macho types

indicators.note: defending means surrounding protectively, so the soldier word encloses the macho types

parts.note: a vet is a veteran
he-men are strong macho men

explanation.surface: A strong veteran stands up for tough guys.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: intense, passionate, showing strong feeling.

clue.text: Posh artist taken with return of star and planet

parts.note: U means upper class, a classic British usage
RA is a Royal Academician

indicators.note: return of means the star word is read backwards

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: An upper-crust painter is linked with a star coming back and a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh world out from the Sun in our solar system.

clue.text: Turned out I should get into a dry wine

indicators.note: should get into places the I inside the other letters

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a non-drinker
red is wine

explanation.surface: I ought to try a dry red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' means dressed, as in well turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well turned out means being nicely dressed in fine clothes.

clue.text: Collapse of the Spanish occupying mount, dejected

indicators.note: occupying means the Spanish article sits inside the mount abbreviation

parts.note: Mt is the abbreviation for mount, a mountain
el is Spanish for the
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A depressed Spaniard takes over a mountain after a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete breakdown or failure, originally of a nuclear reactor core.

clue.text: Like a newspaper's evening edition weather?

definitions.meaning: the late edition is the final one published
to weather a storm is to survive it

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means published last; as one word it means survive longer than.

clue.text: Facing misfortune together like eight during competition?

definitions.meaning: a rowing eight all sit in one shell during a race

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sharing a predicament; literally it is where a racing crew of oarsmen are.

clue.text: French priest overlooking yard in devotional site

indicators.note: overlooking puts the priest above the yard in this down entry

parts.note: abbé is French for a priest

explanation.surface: A French cleric gazes over a yard at a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery or its church, a place of worship.

clue.text: Element of jazz in club

indicators.note: of means the letters are taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: Part of the music is played in a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element of jazz' looks like one musical ingredient; 'Element' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A metallic chemical element, atomic number 30.

clue.text: Bishop among pair in Rome by altar, say, and cross

indicators.note: among means the bishop letters sit between the pair

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
an altar is an example of a table

explanation.surface: A bishop among two Romans beside the altar becomes angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' at the end looks like the Christian symbol beside bishop and altar, but it means annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an irritable person is easily angered, bad-tempered.

clue.text: Air awkward leading question for Baghdad citizen?

indicators.note: awkward implies something clumsy or ill-arranged, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the first question is Question 1, abbreviated Q1, read as QI

explanation.surface: A clumsy, loaded question put to someone from Baghdad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges AIR into IRA; 'leading question' is Q1, the opening question, written with I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital of the country, so its citizens are natives of that land.

clue.text: Characters in revamped 'Dynasty' go round in circles

indicators.note: characters in means the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: People in a remade TV soap Dynasty just keep going round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or air that swirls and whirls in a small circular current.

clue.text: City's teams with training done methodically

indicators.note: with training implies the teams are drilled into a new formation, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A city's sports teams go about their practice in an orderly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with training' rearranges CITYSTEAMS; the possessive 's counts as an S here.
explanation.definitionFit: Carried out according to a fixed plan or method, orderly and thorough.
